items.title: U.S. forces rescue second F-15E crew member from Iran after firefight

featured_image.name: A US F-15 is down in Iran, search and rescue underway

items.description:
U.S. military forces successfully extracted the second crew member of an F-15E Strike Eagle that was shot down over Iran on Friday, capping a tense rescue operation that stretched more than 24 hours and involved firefights with Iranian forces on the ground, according to U.S. officials cited by The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The weapons systems officer had been evading capture in southwestern Iran while Iranian military units and local militia forces combed the area, with Iranian state media broadcasting a bounty of roughly $60,000 for anyone who located the American airmen, according to the BBC. U.S. special operations forces reached the WSO and extracted him in what journalist Jack Murphy, a former Green Beret, described as a "massive firefight" at the recovery site. Al Jazeera reported that a U.S. government representative confirmed the second crew member had been "retrieved" after an "intense exchange of gunfire".[2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: Iran rejects Trump's 48-hour ultimatum as Gulf strikes widen

featured_image.name: Kuwait desalination plant, oil refinery hit by missile and drone strikes

items.description:
Iran's central military command on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's 48-hour ultimatum to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face the destruction of its critical infrastructure, as Tehran continued launching waves of drone and missile strikes across the Gulf and at Israel in the latest escalation of the five-week-old war.

General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi, representing Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, called Trump's threat "a helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action," and warned: "The simple meaning of this message is that the gates of hell will open for you." Trump had written on Truth Social earlier Saturday: "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!"[1][2][3]

items.title: Meloni offers to help rebuild Qatar's war-damaged gas infrastructure

featured_image.name: Italy's Meloni meets Qatar emir to discuss energy issues amid Iran war

items.description:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani at Lusail Palace in Doha on Saturday, offering Italy's support to rebuild Qatar's damaged energy infrastructure as Europe grapples with an energy crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran.[1][2]

Meloni is the first leader from the European Union, NATO, and the G20 to visit the Gulf region since the conflict began on February 28. The unannounced two-day tour, which started in Saudi Arabia on Friday with a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will also include the United Arab Emirates.[3][4][5]
